# B2B Partner Tiers & Member Exclusive Deals

Available on **Advanced, Ultimate** — on **any Shopify plan** (updated 2026-05-25; previously required Shopify Plus B2B, since Shopify opened B2B to non-Plus stores from April 2026). Non-Plus stores are capped at **3 catalogs**; Joy validates against this cap. Plus stores keep unlimited catalogs.

## Why B2B tiers

Designed for business buyers — recognize lifetime company spending, apply benefits at the company level (all account members inherit). Benefits aligned with B2B needs: payment terms, exclusive catalog access, volume discounts.

## Setup

**Joy Admin → Membership → VIP Tiers → Partner tier tab → Add New Tier**:
- **Tier name** (e.g., Silver/Gold/Platinum Partner)
- **Spend threshold** — minimum lifetime spend
- **Start date** — when tracking begins
- **Tier benefits** — discounts, free shipping, catalog access, etc.

Tiers track company lifetime spend and apply automatically to all members of the business account.

---

Available on **Essential, Advanced, Ultimate**.

Set up at **Joy Admin → Membership → Member exclusive deal → Setup**.

## Multiple deals & quantity-based order requirement (added 2026-05-20)

Merchants can now set up and run **multiple Exclusive Deals at the same time** (previously capped at 1 active deal) — e.g. a Black Friday deal, a birth-month bonus deal, and a new-collection promotion can all be live together.

A new order requirement type is available: **"Customer & item quantity limit"** — lets the merchant offer different discount amounts depending on the quantity ordered (discount tiers by quantity), instead of a single flat requirement.

## Active dates

- **Static**: fixed start/end (seasonal, flash)
- **Dynamic** (auto-recurring):
  - Month of birth
  - Weekend
  - Specific day of month (e.g., 15th)
  - Specific day of week (e.g., Mon + Fri)

## Discount types

Discount Amount, Discount Percentage, Free Shipping, Bonus Points.

## Usage limits

Per customer: No limit / Day / Week.

## Customer experience

Members see the deal directly on product pages. Non-members see a CTA inviting them to join the loyalty program to unlock the deal.

# Referral Program

Set up at **Joy Admin → Reward programs → Referrals**. Basic features on All plans; advanced (Shopify customer/order tagging) on Essential, Advanced, Ultimate.

## Reward types

| For | Available reward types |
|---|---|
| **Referee** (new customer) | Points, Store credit, Discount %, Discount amount |
| **Referrer** | Points, **Points (based on order value)**, Store credit (fixed), Store credit (% of referee order), Discount %, Discount amount |

**Points based on order value (added 2026-08-10):** set at **Reward method → Points based on order value**. Merchant enters a points-per-$1 rate applied to the referee's order **subtotal after discount** (shipping and tax excluded) and chooses a rounding rule; a preview shows an example calculation. This exists so a merchant running a points-based loyalty program can reward referrers proportionally without granting Store Credit permissions they may not want to give.

- **Tier-based rewards** — Customize referrer reward by VIP tier. For the points-based-on-order-value method, turning this on switches the setup screen from a single preview number to a reminder to set a rate for each tier individually.
- **Max amount cap on % discount** — e.g., "15% off, up to $30" — set independently per side, off by default
- The configured rate shows to customers on the Referral block of **Widget V4**, e.g. *"2 points per $1 your friend spends."*

## Referral redirection URL

Default = homepage. Change to any landing page (e.g., a campaign page).

## Sharing channels

Customers share their unique link via the loyalty widget across selected social/email channels. Email invite (see next chunk) is built-in.

---

## Flow

1. Referrer shares their unique link
2. Referee clicks link → lands on referral page → enters email to claim → **7-day cookie** stored on device → activity = pending. The **referee's** reward (coupon / store credit) is issued at this claim step; the **referrer's** reward stays pending until the referee actually orders.
3. Referee places order with the **same email** → activity = complete on thank-you page → both rewarded.

**When the referrer's reward is granted** — the referrer is rewarded only after the referee places a qualifying order, following the shop's earn-status setting (same as points earning):

- **Reward on Paid** (default, `earnByOrderStatus = financial_status`): granted as soon as the referee's order is **Paid**.
- **Reward on Fulfilled / Partial**: the reward waits until the order reaches that fulfilment status. While the order is Paid but not yet fulfilled, the referral shows **"Awaiting fulfilment"** (this is normal — it means the order was placed and is waiting to fulfil, not that something failed).

## Troubleshooting (referrer didn't get reward)

- **Different emails** — referee used different email at claim vs checkout. Both sides need same email
- **App pixel disabled** — check **Shopify Admin → Settings → Customer Events → Joy** is enabled. Toggle program off/on to re-sync
- Cookie expired (>7 days between click and purchase)

## Common false negatives when testing

- **"Running in test mode" message** means the referral program is in **Sandbox / preview** — go live for real rewards to be issued.
- **Same PC / same browser:** on a device where the merchant is logged into their own store, the referral page may show only the code without prompting for a friend's email. Test in incognito, another account, or a phone to see the real behaviour.

## Anti-cheat

Built-in fraud prevention stops customers gaming the program with multiple accounts. Configure limits per program in the referral settings. When anti-cheat is enabled, a referral is blocked when the referrer and referee share the **same browser, same email, or same IP address**, or reuse the **same order**. The referee's order must also have a **subtotal greater than $0** — a $0 order does not qualify the referrer for a reward.

## Referral limits

- **Referral limit per customer** (field label in **Joy Admin → Reward programs → Referrals → referral settings**) — caps the number of successful referrals a single referrer can earn from. Example: set to 5 to let each member earn rewards from a maximum of 5 successful referrals; combine with a fixed per-referral reward (e.g. store credit or points equivalent to a fixed amount) to naturally cap the total a member can earn.
- **Plan-based limit** — the **Free plan** caps how many referral orders can be rewarded. To lift the cap, the merchant upgrades to a paid plan. Higher plans raise or remove this limit.

## Reward revocation on refund

If the referee's qualifying order is **fully refunded**, the referrer's reward is **automatically revoked** when the merchant has enabled **Auto-revoke referrer reward** on the referral program (points are deducted back and a revoke activity is logged). If the setting is off, the referrer keeps the reward even after a refund.

---

Available on **All plans**. Referrer enters friend's email in the widget → system auto-sends a branded invitation email containing the referrer's name, the discount/reward, and the referral link.

Delivery channels supported:
- Joy's built-in email
- Klaviyo
- Shopify Flow

When the friend purchases, both sides get rewards + confirmation emails.

## Merchant referral program (refer-a-merchant)

This is a **separate program from the customer referral program above** — here the merchant refers other Shopify merchants to Joy, not customers referring friends.

- **Set up:** No setup needed by the merchant. Eligible merchants see a banner "Referral Program" on the **Homepage** or **Settings → Subscription** page, and get a unique referral code/link to share with other Shopify merchants.
- **Eligibility:** Banner + program only shows to merchants who meet eligibility requirements (see Joy's merchant referral program guide for the current criteria).
- **Reward (referrer merchant) — Joy credit toward their next billing cycle**, tiered by the referrer's plan: **$29** on Essential, **$90** on Advanced, **$250** on Ultimate, per successful referral.
- **Reward (referred merchant):** discount off their first 3 months — 50% on Essential, 30% on Advanced, 20% on Ultimate.
- **Milestone bonus** (Advanced + Ultimate referrers only): extra **+$30** at 2 referrals, **+$100** at 5 referrals, **+$300** at 10 referrals.
- **Why it exists:** Joy's paid-ads/CAC channel for acquiring merchants was costly and underperforming, so merchant-to-merchant referral was added as a cheaper acquisition channel (added 2026-05-25).

# Translations

## Plan availability

| Feature | Plans |
|---|---|
| Edit English content | All |
| Change default language + edit content | All (including Free) |
| Detect Language tab (view-only — see detected language per visitor) | All |
| Add languages (add additional languages beyond the default) | Essential, Advanced, Ultimate |

## Surfaces translated

- Loyalty widget (popup) ✅
- Loyalty page (embedded) ✅
- Account page (Loyalty Hub) ✅
- Checkout page (Shopify checkout extensions) ✅
- Apple Wallet & Google Wallet passes ✅

Joy stands out by translating **checkout extensions and customer account UI** — many other loyalty apps cannot.

## Coverage

38 supported languages, all fully customizable — every label, message, button text editable to match brand voice.

---

## Setup

**Joy Admin → Settings → Translations** → choose default language (available on all plans, including Free). The **Detected Language** tab is visible on all plans (view-only — shows detected language by IP/browser per visitor). Adding additional languages beyond the default requires Essential plan or above.

### Detected Language — no cap on number of languages

The Detected Language list has no limit on how many languages can appear — a previous cap of 5 detected languages has been removed, so merchants selling across many markets (e.g. EU) can have as many as needed detected/added.

## Editing

Pick the language → edit any label/message/button per surface. Save. Updates apply to live storefront immediately.

### Editing widget text specifically (e.g. "Membership card", "Receive exclusive offers...")

Two routes reach the same underlying widget strings — either works:

- **Settings → Translations** → pick language → **Widget design** surface → pick the block (e.g. **Membership card**) → edit the label text.
- **On-site content → Widget → Widget design → Setup** (the widget editor) → left sidebar **Settings → Content & Translations** — inline editor for all widget text labels, with **Revert to default** and **On-brand** (AI-rewrite) buttons.

If the merchant is asking about wording, not styling, either path fixes it — no design/CSS change needed.

## Known limitations

- Translations entered on the **Classic** widget carry over when switching to **Unified** — no re-entry needed.
- Some strings, specifically **VIP tier descriptions inside Customer Accounts**, can show untranslated and may need manual entry; log a gap if a surface won't translate.
- **Redeem-reward product names cannot be translated through Joy.** When a reward is tied to a specific Shopify product, the name shown to customers is pulled directly from that product's title in Shopify — it isn't a Joy-editable label. To show it in another language, translate the product's title itself (e.g. via Shopify's own product-title translation / Translate & Adapt on the product), not through Joy's Translations settings.

## Checkout limitation

Shopify Checkout UI extensions don't support i18n by IP/browser. You can only set **one default language** at the checkout level via Theme Editor. The rest of Joy (widget, loyalty page, account page) supports auto-detect normally.

# Email Marketing & SMS Integrations

Available on **All plans**. Connect at **Joy Admin → Integrations → [app]**.

## Supported

| App | Connection method |
|---|---|
| Klaviyo | OAuth |
| Omnisend | OAuth/API key |
| Mailchimp | OAuth |
| Drip | API key |
| Sendlane | API Token |
| PushOwl | OAuth |

## Two layers of integration

1. **Basic data sync** — Customer profile fields: points balance, tier, member status, referral link, birthday — used for segmentation/personalization
2. **Real-time event triggers** — Loyalty events streamed to the marketing tool for automation flows (Klaviyo and Omnisend have richest event support)

---

Both have the strongest event integration. Once connected:

## Customer profile properties synced

- Points balance
- VIP tier
- Member status (member/guest/left)
- Referral link
- Birthday

Use these in **Klaviyo segments** or **Omnisend segments** to target campaigns (e.g., "All Gold-tier customers", "Customers with > 500 points").

## Omnisend sync details

Omnisend receives the **same customer profile properties as Klaviyo** — points balance, VIP tier, member status, referral link and birthday — kept in sync automatically as they change in Joy, usable the same way in Omnisend segments and automations.

If a recent change (e.g. a tier-threshold update) doesn't seem to have reflected yet in Omnisend, there's a manual **Sync Again** button in the Omnisend integration settings rather than waiting for the next automatic sync pass.

## Klaviyo email template variables (profile properties)

Use these exact `person|lookup` variables in Klaviyo email templates / dynamic blocks. Source: help.joy.so. These are the only variables Joy supports for Klaviyo; do not suggest any other variable format.

| Data | Klaviyo variable |
|---|---|
| Points balance | `{{ person\|lookup:'Joy Loyalty Points'\|default:'' }}` |
| VIP tier | `{{ person\|lookup:'Joy Vip tier'\|default:'' }}` |
| Member status | `{{ person\|lookup:'Joy member status'\|default:'' }}` |
| Referral link | `{{ person\|lookup:'Joy Referral URL'\|default:'' }}` |
| Birthday | `{{ person\|lookup:'Birthday'\|default:'' }}` |

Profile properties update in real time when points / tier / membership change in Joy.

### Event properties (in Klaviyo flows triggered by Joy events)
Use `event|lookup` (not `person|lookup`) for data carried by the triggering event:
`{{ event\|lookup:'Property name'\|default:'' }}`
Example: `You have {{ event\|lookup:'Customer points'\|default:'0' }} points`

Joy event triggers: `Joy: Earn Point`, `Joy: Redeem Points`, `Joy: Tier Achieved`, `Joy: Points Eligible Reward`, `Joy: Birthday`, `Joy: 7 Days Pre Point Expiration`.

## Event triggers

Real-time events stream to the marketing tool, usable in automated flows:
- Earn points
- Redeem points
- Tier reached
- Coupon issued
- Points expiring
- Birthday approaching
- Referral completed

Build event-based flows: "When Joy 'Tier reached' fires → send welcome email + 10% off coupon".

---

## Connection

- **Mailchimp** — OAuth, syncs customer + loyalty fields for audience segmentation and automation
- **Drip** — API key. Syncs Point Balance, Member Status, Referral link, VIP Tier, Birthday
- **Sendlane** — API Token (from Sendlane → Account → API → Sendlane API V2). Pick a list to sync. Same fields as Drip
- **PushOwl** — OAuth. Push-notification triggers for: 7 days before birthday, Birthday, Point expiration (7 + 3 days prior), Eligible for reward, Point activity (earned/redeemed)

## Klaviyo disconnect warning banner

Joy auto-detects when a store's **Klaviyo connection has disconnected** (e.g. token revoked, app uninstalled/reconnected on the Klaviyo side) and shows a warning banner on the **Joy Admin → Home** page prompting the merchant to reconnect.

Why this matters for support: previously a silent Klaviyo disconnect was invisible to the merchant — email flows kept "running" on stale/no data, and merchants would report symptoms like **"emails aren't sending"** or **"points/tier show as 0 in my Klaviyo emails"** with no obvious cause. The real cause was the integration being disconnected, not a bug in the sync or the email content.

If a merchant reports missing/zeroed loyalty data in Klaviyo emails or automations:
1. Check whether they've noticed a warning banner on Joy's Home page — if so, that confirms Klaviyo is currently disconnected; have them reconnect via **Integrations → Klaviyo**.
2. Even if they say they haven't seen a banner, still verify **Integrations → Klaviyo** shows "Connected" as a troubleshooting step — banners can be missed or the disconnect may have happened and been reconnected since, requiring a fresh check.

## Troubleshooting: Klaviyo events/variables

**Joy events/metrics not showing in Klaviyo (need to re-add triggers)**
- Confirm **Integrations → Klaviyo** is Connected. The available Joy metrics are `Joy: Earn Point`, `Joy: Redeem Points`, `Joy: Tier Achieved`, `Joy: Points Eligible Reward`, `Joy: Birthday`, `Joy: 7 Days Pre Point Expiration`.
- If the metrics don't appear, **disconnect and reconnect** Klaviyo (generates a fresh API key) to re-stream events, then re-check.
- Still missing after reconnect → escalate with store URL + screenshot of Klaviyo metrics. Append `<escalate_human>`.

**Variable shows `n/a` or the wrong value in a Klaviyo email**
- Almost always the wrong **lookup type**. Data sitting on the **profile** uses `person|lookup` (e.g. `{{ person|lookup:'Joy Loyalty Points'|default:'' }}`). Data carried by the **triggering event** (bonus points on an Earn/Tier flow) uses `event|lookup` (e.g. `{{ event|lookup:'Customer points'|default:'0' }}`). Using `person|lookup` for event data returns `n/a`.
- Confirm the customer actually has the data in Joy and that the Klaviyo profile shows Joy properties. If syntax and data are correct but the value is still wrong, escalate with store URL + email preview + Klaviyo profile + Joy customer screenshots. Append `<escalate_human>`.

**Coupon reminder now carries the coupon name too**
Coupon reminder event triggers carry `{{ event.coupon_name }}` in addition to the coupon code, so templates can reference the reward's display name rather than just the code.

**Tier email shows the wrong/previous tier (timing issue)**
Profile properties sync asynchronously, so a "you've reached a new tier" email can send while Klaviyo still holds the customer's *previous* tier — the email ends up announcing one tier but listing another tier's rewards. Until the permanent fix ships, use the **event** properties instead of the profile property for tier-reach emails:
- `{{ event|lookup:'New tier name'|default:'' }}`
- `{{ event|lookup:'Current tier name'|default:'' }}`

These pull the tier at the exact moment the event fires and are accurate immediately.

**Known limitations (log as feature requests, don't promise a fix)**
- There is **no dedicated "Reward Expiring" Klaviyo event** — Joy syncs `coupon_expiry_date` as a profile property only.

- kb_notifications (Joy's own email notifications)
- kb_referral (referral email invite via Klaviyo)

# Earning Programs

All earning programs live at **Joy Admin → Reward programs → Earning programs → Add rule**.

> To set up a **"spend = points" rate** (e.g. 1 currency spent = 10 points), the program is **Place order**: open **Reward programs → Place order** and set the earning rate there. "Per amount spent" is a *rate option inside the Place order rule* (alongside "per item purchased" and "per order") — it lives under the Place order program, so the full path is **Reward programs → Place order → per amount spent rate**.

| Program | Plans | What it rewards |
|---|---|---|
| Place order | All | Points or store credit per purchase |
| Place subscription | All | Recurring subscription orders |
| Sign up | All | Joining the loyalty program — granted via 3 paths: storefront (log in + active embed widget), widget popup join, or POS (guest→member). See "Sign up reward — how it's earned" below. Leaving an email alone does not qualify; applies to all account types |
| Sign up newsletters | All | Subscribing to newsletter (Shopify marketing status must be "subscribed", not "pending") |
| Birthday reward | Essential, Advanced, Ultimate | Customer's birthday |
| Member anniversary | Advanced, Ultimate | Days since signup (e.g., 365 = 1 year) |
| Write review | Pro and above | Product reviews via Klaviyo, Air, Judge.me, Loox, Okendo, Reviews.io, Stamped, Fera, Yotpo, Growave |
| Social activity | Essential, Advanced, Ultimate | Follows, likes, shares on social platforms |
| Instagram comment / story reply / story mention / live comment | Advanced, Ultimate | Specific Instagram interactions (Business or Creator account required) |
| Google reviews | Essential, Advanced, Ultimate | Reviews on Google Places — admin approves before points granted |
| Fill out a survey | All | Survey completion via Shopify Flow |
| Visit website | All | Customer visits to store |
| Streak bonus challenge | All | Consecutive-day visits with milestone bonuses |
| Custom program | Advanced and above | Custom triggers — visit specific page, custom event, Shopify Flow |
| Submit receipt | Advanced and above | Photo of purchase receipt — admin approves |
| Submit form | Advanced and above | Proof of off-platform actions (TikTok, UGC, etc.) via custom form |

---

## Sign up reward — how it's earned

The Sign up reward is **not** granted the moment a Shopify account is created. It is awarded through one of **3 trigger paths**, and the customer must pass all eligibility rules.

**Eligibility (all must be true):**
1. Sign up program is **live** (not Sandbox).
2. Customer has **not earned it before** — one-time only, protected against double-earn.
3. **Account created on/after the program started** — the customer's account-created date must be ≥ the program's start date (shown as "Start date" / "Period" on the Sign up program). The Sign up program also only applies to **"New account sign ups"**.
   - This is why **customers who already had an account before the program was turned on do NOT earn it.**
   - If the merchant wants existing/older customers to earn it too, this requires an internal adjustment — **escalate to the team** (do not promise a self-serve setting).
4. Not blocked by shop config: **manual member assignment** mode or an **excluded segment** will skip the reward.

**The 3 ways it triggers:**

| Path | How it fires |
|---|---|
| **Online store (widget)** | Customer **logs in** to a customer account, then loads any storefront page where the **Joy embed widget is active**. The widget auto-detects the logged-in customer and grants the reward — no button click needed. Leaving an email only (form / checkout / newsletter) does **not** qualify, and a logged-out guest does not qualify. |
| **Widget popup "Join"** | Customer opens the Joy widget and joins → the reward is granted (skipped if manual member assignment is on). |
| **POS** | Customer buys at POS and is identified as a member (guest → member) → the Sign up reward is granted automatically. Separate from the storefront path. |

**Note:** Creating the account alone (Shopify customer create/update) does not earn the reward — the customer earns it later via one of the 3 paths above.

---

## Reward methods

- **Per amount spent**: 1 point per $1
- **One-time at threshold**: 100 points when order ≥ $50
- **Per item quantity**: 5 points per item
- **Fixed per order**: 10 points per order

---

## Different earning rates per VIP tier (points multiplier)

A merchant can give each VIP tier its own earning rate — e.g. **1.5 points per $1 for a
mid tier and 2 points per $1 for the top tier**. This is built into the **Place an order**
program. It does **not** need Shopify Flow, and it does **not** need the Rule Engine.

**Requirement:** the shop must already have a **VIP Tier program set up and enabled**
(VIP Tiers is available on any paid plan). If VIP Tiers isn't set up, the tier option on
the Place-order program is greyed out with the note *"You haven't setup VIP Tier yet"* —
set up the tiers first.

**How to set it up:**

1. Go to **Joy Admin → Reward programs → Earning programs → Place an order**
2. Find the **"Who to reward"** options and select
   **"Only customers in a VIP tier can earn points"**
3. The form then shows **one earning-rate field per tier** — enter each tier's own rate
   (e.g. 1.5 points per $1 for the mid tier, 2 points per $1 for the top tier)
4. **Save**

Each tier now earns at its own rate, and a customer earns at the rate of whichever tier
they are currently in.

---

## Place order program templates (Rule Engine required)

When adding a **Place order** program, merchants can pick a **pre-built template** instead of starting from a blank 1pt/$1 form. Templates cover common patterns: **VIP-tier-based rates**, **subscription bonus**, and **birthday bonus** — picking one auto-fills the program's settings, which the merchant can still edit afterward.

**Where:** Reward programs → Add program → Place order → template picker screen.

**Requirement:** template picker is only available when the shop has the **Rule Engine enabled**. Without Rule Engine, Place order programs are still created from a blank form as before.

---

## Reward type

- **Points** — abstract units, redeemed for discount coupons
- **Store credit** — real $ value, applied at checkout. Joy prompts inline for Shopify permission on first use; one-time grant covers all programs

## Multi-currency earning rates (Advanced, Ultimate)

Toggle **Apply different rates by currency** in Reward settings. Joy reads the **presentment currency** customer paid in. Set rates proportional to FX rates so reward value stays consistent.

## Conditions ("Check if")

**Recipe — earn only on full-price items (exclude sale items):** keep sale items in a dedicated collection (e.g. "SALE"), set the Place-order rule's product condition to **exclude** that collection, and mirror the same restriction on the redeeming program's **Applicable categories** so redemption doesn't stack on discounted items.


Customer / Order / Product / Collection — combine with **All** or **Any** logic. Common use: exclude orders by tag (e.g., orders from non-Shopify platforms).

## Place-order earning blocked outside the program conditions

Besides the per-program "Check if" conditions, a Place-order reward can be withheld by shop-level settings that sit **outside** the program:

- **Order filter (Settings → Order)** — separate from the program's product/collection conditions. An order can be excluded by **order tag**, **source name** (Web / POS / Draft), or **payment gateway**, or by "exclude orders without a customer". If a merchant excludes an order this way, no place-order points are awarded even if the program conditions match.
- **B2B / company orders** — when the shop's loyalty eligibility is set to exclude B2B, orders placed on a company/B2B profile are logged but earn no points.
- **Opt-in enrollment (guest not joined)** — Joy has three membership-enrollment modes, set at **Settings → General → "Membership enrollment"**: **Auto-enroll** (customer becomes a member automatically), **Manual** (merchant assigns membership), and **Opt-in enrollment** — under Opt-in, logging into a Shopify account is not enough to become a member: the customer stays a **guest** (sees guest view) until they actively click **"Join"** at a loyalty touchpoint (the widget, account page, or loyalty page). A guest who hasn't joined does not earn place-order points until they join (their activity shows "order recorded", not "placed order"). Merchants use Opt-in when they want to target only customers who show real interest, rather than crediting every passer-by who happens to have an account.

## Trust-based earning not awarded (visit / social / Google review)

For Visit website, social, Instagram, and Google review programs, the customer must be **logged in** when performing the action. **Google review** points sit in a **pending/approval queue** the merchant must approve before they are granted. **Instagram** needs an IG Business/Creator account connected and the customer's IG username linked.

## Fraud prevention

- Max earning per rule per customer
- **Earning frequency limit** — set under the program's Anti-cheat → "Set earning points limit". Options are labeled **"every 24 hours / every 7 days / every 30 days / every 365 days"** (help text: "in the last X days", with a tooltip example). These are **rolling windows measured from the customer's last qualifying action** — e.g. "every 7 days" means 7 days after they last earned, not a calendar week that resets every Monday. (Older UI showed "Day / Week / Month / Year" — same rolling-window behavior, just clearer wording now; merchants who set it up before shouldn't expect a calendar-week reset.)
- Auto-revoke on cancelled/refunded orders

## Calculation notes

- Shipping and taxes are NOT included by default (toggle "Reward for additional fee" to include them)
- Calculated on order subtotal in primary currency unless multi-currency is on

---

## Birthday reward (Essential+)

- **Date format**: MM/DD/YYYY or DD/MM/YYYY
- **Delivery**: Automatic (system grants) or Manual (customer claims)
- **Timing**: Exact birthday, calendar month, or custom range (X days before/after)
- Optional: grant reward N days before exact birthday
- Customer must have a birthday on file — see kb_birthday for how to collect

## Member anniversary (Advanced+)

Reward N days after customer joined loyalty program. Common: 30 days, 6 months, 365 days. Reward types: Points, Discount %, Discount amount. Customers see/claim from their loyalty page.

---

## Generic social activity (Essential+)

Trust-based — Joy can't verify completion via social APIs. Customer is guided to the URL; most follow through.

## Instagram programs (Advanced, Ultimate)

All require **Instagram Business or Creator account** + connection in **Joy Admin → Integrations → Instagram** (one connection covers all IG programs). Customers must link their Instagram username in the widget.

| Event | Detail |
|---|---|
| Comment on Instagram | Tracks comments on selected posts |
| Story reply | Text replies only — emoji-only reactions filtered out |
| Story mention | Customer mentions your brand in their story (24h window) |
| Live comment | Comments during your IG Live |

Stories require the Instagram mobile app. Detection happens while content is live.

**AI auto-reply on comments (reduces Meta "Artificial Engagement" risk):** the Instagram comment program can auto-reply to customer comments to grant points, configured at **Instagram comment rewards → reply settings**. It supports **reply variety** — either a random pick from a list of reply texts, or AI-generated replies based on the comment's context — instead of one fixed sentence, plus a **per-post reply limit (default 5 replies/post)**. This exists because posting the same auto-reply repeatedly on one post can get flagged by Meta as "Artificial Engagement" (merchants have had accounts suspended over this) — a policy warning banner shows when auto-reply is enabled. Merchants should keep reply variety on and the per-post limit reasonably low rather than raising it freely.

Connects to your review app: Klaviyo, Air Reviews, Judge.me, Loox, Okendo, Reviews.io, Stamped, Fera, Yotpo, Growave. See kb_integrations-reviews for per-app setup.

**Scoping to specific products/collections:** the Write review program (and Milestone review) can be scoped to **all products / selected products / selected collections / all except a collection** — it no longer has to apply to every product. Merchants use this to promote reviews on a specific product or collection (e.g. a new launch) instead of store-wide.

- Enter your Google Places URL
- After customer leaves a review, merchant sees it in **Activities** panel
- **Earning points** = approve before granting; **Instant points** = grant immediately

Connects via **Shopify Flow**. Merchant clicks **Create Shopify flow** → flow links survey completion (e.g., Zigpoll) to point reward.

Set points per visit + a frequency limit — labeled **"every 24 hours / every 7 days / every 30 days / every 365 days"** — which is a **rolling window from the customer's last visit-earn**, not a calendar day/week/month reset (see Fraud prevention above for the full explanation). Pair with **Visit Website Popup** in Branding for on-site prompt.

Enhanced visit program — daily points + bonus on streak completion. Drives habit-forming engagement.

Triggers beyond defaults: **Visit a page** (URL exact or contains), **Custom events**, **Shopify Flow** triggers. Build your own logic.

Customizable proof form for off-platform actions (TikTok hashtag posts, UGC, external reviews). Optional **Instant reward** gives small points on submit before review.

# Loyalty Widget & Branding

## Classic widget vs Unified widget

Joy launched the **Unified widget** as a complete rebuild of the storefront loyalty UI.

| | Classic widget | Unified widget |
|---|---|---|
| **Who has it** | Merchants who installed Joy before the Unified launch | Merchants who installed Joy after the Unified widget launch |
| **Status badge** | "Classic is live" | "Unified widget — Live" |
| **Focus** | Points and rewards only | All-in-one: profile, orders, wishlist, recommendations, points, rewards, and more |
| **Design editor** | 4 horizontal tabs (Widget theme / Membership card / Display / Advanced) | Full sidebar editor with live storefront preview |
| **Customization** | Limited color/font options | Every color, font, spacing, border radius exposed as CSS properties — full brand control |
| **Performance** | Standard | Lazy-loaded, smaller bundle on first paint |
| **Data** | — | Same Joy data — programs, points, customers carry over untouched |

## How to check which widget you're on

**Joy Admin → On-site content → Widget → Widget design** section — it shows two cards, **Unified widget** and **Classic widget**:
- Badge says **"Classic is live"** → you're on Classic
- Badge says **"Unified is live"** on the Unified card → you're on Unified

## Switching from Classic to Unified

Merchants on Classic can switch at any time:
- **Joy Admin → On-site content → Widget → Widget design → Switch to Unified** button (at the Widget design section heading)
- All existing Joy data (points, programs, customers) carries over — nothing is lost
- Both versions never run simultaneously

## Free setup offer

When a merchant asks about the difference or expresses interest in switching, offer the free setup service:

> "We're offering a free setup service where our team styles your unified loyalty widget or loyalty page to match your store's branding, colors, layout — the whole thing. You won't need to lift a finger. We'll take care of it and send you the result to review. Do you want to give it a try?"

If merchant accepts → collect store URL and escalate to team with `<escalate_human>`.

## Classic widget — features still on Classic only

Milestone program UI, interactive website popup, Wallet pass / QR, Submit receipt program, branded reminder popup — these auto-fallback to Classic UI even on Unified stores.

---

## How to identify Widget v4

The easiest tell: go to **Joy Admin → On-site content → Widget → Setup**. 
- **V4**: opens a full **Widget design editor** with a left sidebar (Settings / Header / Body / Footer / Extensions / Advanced) and a live storefront preview on the right.
- **V3**: opens a page with 4 horizontal tabs (Widget theme / Membership card / Display / Advanced settings).

## Widget design editor — path

**Joy Admin → On-site content → Widget → Widget design → Setup**

## Sidebar structure

### Settings
- **Design** — Preset Theme (Midnight, Forest, Ocean, Warm, Blush, Minimal, Dark, Slate) + Industry inspiration presets (Fashion, Beauty & Wellness, Food & Drink, Home & Garden, Sports & Fitness, Pets & Animals, Men's Grooming, Default), Primary color, Background color, Layout (Widget / Drawer), Position on desktop, Earn & Redeem layout (Tabs / Separate blocks), Text size, Border radius (None / Sharp / Soft / Rounded / Extra), Currency icon (None / Emoji / Image), Fonts (Heading + Body), Text theme colors, Buttons (color, text color, text case), Cards (heading/body text color, background, border)
- **Launcher** — Float button style (Icon only / Label only / Icon & label / Point balance), Point balance label, Label section color, Button size (S/M/L/XL), Border radius (Pill/Rounded/Square), Alignment (Bottom left / Bottom right)
- **Content & Translations** — inline editor to customize all widget text labels (Program name, Launcher, Guest view, Logged in, Points display, Tier perks, Program tabs, Section titles, Coupons, Referral, Redeem flow, Earn flow, bundle chip templates like `Save {{value}} · {{type}}`, etc.). Buttons: **Revert to default** (reset all text) and **On-brand** (AI-rewrite labels to match store voice).

### Header
- **Header** — Program name text size (Small/Medium/Large), Header background color (or "Use primary"), Header text color, Logo (Add image, or paste image URL, or "Use store logo" button — any aspect ratio, height configurable), Header background image (upload; recommended **8:5 ratio, 800×500px, under 200KB**) + overlay opacity slider

### Body
Each block can be **toggled on/off** and **drag-and-drop reordered**. Click any block to edit its content, text, or images inline.

| Block | Notes |
|---|---|
| Membership card | Card layout (Compact/Classic), Default avatar, Guest card image, Member card image, Sign-in settings, Open widget after login |
| My coupons | — |

**Membership card custom blocks** — click the `+` under Membership card to add: Heading, Rich text, Button, Divider, Image banner, Image with text, Custom link, Custom CTA.

- **Footer menu** — bottom navigation tabs. Drag to reorder, toggle visibility, customize each tab.
  - **Display mode**: Icons & labels / Icons only / Labels only

  - Tabs: **Home, Rewards, Orders, Wishlist, Reviews, Profile** (each toggleable; Wishlist/Reviews hidden by default)

## SMS/WhatsApp marketing consent in Profile

The Unified widget's **Profile → Settings** sub-page lets customers opt in to SMS/WhatsApp marketing directly from the widget, without leaving the storefront.

- **Where:** Widget → **Profile → Settings**.
- **Flow:** the customer enters their phone number and toggles consent to receive SMS/WhatsApp messages. If the customer has no phone number on file yet, they first see an **"Add your phone"** prompt in Account info — once a number is saved, the consent toggle becomes available.
- **What Joy does:** Joy writes the consent to the customer's record on **Shopify**, so the merchant can use it for marketing/automation (e.g. segments, flows).
- **What Joy does NOT do:** Joy does not send the SMS/WhatsApp messages itself — actual sending still goes through whatever SMS/WhatsApp platform the merchant already has connected. Joy's role here is only to capture and store the consent.

### Extensions
Toggle on/off: **Wishlist**, **Bundling**, **Reviews**, **Subscription**, **Survey**. Each extension that needs a companion app (e.g. Wishlist) shows an "Install app / Watch setup guide / Verify installation" panel and a layout/options block (e.g. Wishlist layout: Carousel / Grid / List, image hover effect). The Wishlist extension auto-detects **Joy Wishlist**, **Swym Wishlist Plus**, or **Wishlist King** — whichever wishlist app the store has installed — with no extra config needed to pick the provider.

### Advanced
- **Display** — hide widget from guests, page restriction, instant popup, hide widget button
- **Popup** — popup behavior settings

## Show External Discounts in My Coupons

Joy can surface discount codes that were **not created by Joy** — e.g. codes made directly in Shopify, or by another app like Klaviyo — inside the widget's **My Coupons** section, next to the customer's regular Joy coupons. This solves the case where a merchant wants a non-Joy discount to be visible to customers in the loyalty widget.

- **Where to enable:** Widget design editor → **Advanced → External discounts**.
- **Default:** off.
- **Limit:** the merchant selects up to **10** discount codes to show.
- **Eligibility:** Joy only displays a selected code to customers who actually qualify for it (matching the discount's own audience — All customers / Specific customers / Segment — and whether it's still within its active dates and usage limit). Each visible code shows its value and conditions.
- This is a Unified widget feature; it lives in the same Advanced tab as Display/Popup/Custom CSS settings.

## Live preview controls

The editor's right pane is a live storefront preview with an **"Embed active"** status badge. The "Preview as" toolbar lets the merchant simulate different viewers without affecting the live store:
- **Device** — Desktop / Mobile
- **Customer** — Signed in / Guest
- **VIP tier** — Member (no VIP) / Simulate VIP active
- **Customise customer data…** — set sample points/tier for the preview

**Steps:**
1. Open **Joy Admin → On-site content → Widget → Widget design → Setup**.
2. In the left sidebar, navigate to Sections ⛶,  click the **Header** or the **Body block** that contains the image you want to change (e.g. Header logo, Header background image, Membership card → Default avatar / Guest card / Member card image, or an Image banner / Image with text custom block) (https://capture.avada.io/i/3MlO1vlvJ8z3).
3. In the editor (middle pane), find that image's field and click **Upload image** (or paste an image URL) to replace it. The live preview on the right updates immediately.

# VIP Tiers

Available on **Advanced, Ultimate**. Configure at **Joy Admin → Membership → VIP Tiers**.

## Tier calculation rules

| Rule | Best for |
|---|---|
| **Points earned** | Encourage broad engagement (purchases + reviews + referrals) |
| **Amount spent** | Reward high spenders |
| **Number of orders** | Reward repeat purchase frequency |

> Redeeming/spending points lowers the active points balance and can **demote** a customer on **Points earned** tiers. To keep redemption from demoting customers, use **Amount spent** (cumulative spend is not reduced by redemptions) or assign protected customers to an **Exclusive tier**.

## Per-tier points-earning rate

A VIP tier can carry a **points-earning multiplier** as a perk, so higher tiers earn points faster (for example Bronze 1pt/$1, Silver 2×, Gold 3×). Configure it as a tier privilege; the storefront shows the earning rate for the customer's current logged-in tier. The **Bonus Points** perk accepts **whole multipliers only** (2×, 3×, 4×) — fractional rates such as 1.5× are not available in this field.

**For a fractional/decimal rate (e.g. 1.5×), use the Rule Engine instead**: upgrade the Earning program to Rule Engine (**Reward programs → Earning programs → More actions**), then set a **Place order** rule with the decimal rate targeted at that tier — either give the rule **"Who to reward" = "Only customers in a VIP tier can earn points"** (one rate field per tier) or add a Rule Engine condition for the tier segment. Requires a VIP Tier program already set up and enabled, and Rule Engine is on **Advanced and Ultimate**. You do **not** need Shopify Flow for this — earlier guidance suggesting a Flow bridge for decimal rates is superseded; kb_earning-programs has the full walkthrough.

The alternative mechanism is a **segment-targeted earning rule** in the Rule engine (Customer segment → Bonus for VIP tier or tagged customers) when you want finer targeting.

> If the earning value shown in the popup does not match the tier setting, collect the customer email + tier + a screenshot and escalate — a display mismatch has been logged to tech before.

Discount code prefix must follow `ABCD-` format.

## Per-tier configuration

- **Tier name** — branded (e.g., "Beauty Enthusiast")
- **Threshold** — points/$/orders required
- **Entry reward** (one-time on tier reach by default; can be re-granted on re-reach — see "Re-grant entry reward after downgrade" below): Discount amount/%, Bonus points, Free product, Free shipping, BXGY
- **Privileges/perks** (ongoing while in tier) — set up under **Membership → VIP Tiers → [tier] → Tier privileges → Add perks**
- **Pre-Tier reward** — coupon when customer reaches tier threshold

**Set up a tier entry reward (exact menu path):** Joy Admin → Membership → VIP Tiers → [select the tier, e.g. Bronze] → **Entry reward** → Add reward → choose type (Free product / Discount / Bonus points / Free shipping / BXGY) → Save → **Launch** to apply.

⚠️ The entry-reward coupon (e.g. "Free socks" on reaching Bronze) is created under **Entry reward** — NOT under Tier privileges/Benefits. If a configured entry-reward coupon is "not appearing", confirm it was added under Entry reward (not Privileges) and that the tier was re-Launched after editing.

---

Starter plan merchants can fully configure the **basic** VIP tier setup in trial mode (tier names, thresholds, entry rewards, visuals) — saved configurations persist forever and activate with one click after upgrade. Cannot launch to customers and cannot activate notifications until a paid plan with VIP Tiers is active.

> Note: this trial-mode configuration covers the **standard tier setup only**. It does **not** include **Tier Assessment / rolling-window maintenance**, which is an Advanced/Ultimate feature and additionally requires Joy support to enable (see "Tier Assessment" below). A free-plan merchant cannot set up a rolling-year tier assessment.

---

**Privileges** (perks) apply automatically on **every qualifying order** while customer holds the tier. Different from **Entry Rewards** which fire once when first reaching the tier.

**Set up a perk (exact menu path):** Joy Admin → **Membership** → **VIP Tiers** → [select the tier, e.g. Gold] → **Tier privileges** → **Add perks** → choose a privilege type (Discount / Free Shipping / Free Product / Bonus Points / Exclusive Products / Custom Reward) → configure the value → **Save** → **Launch** the tier to apply. Repeat **Add perks** to stack more than one perk in the same tier.

**If a perk isn't applying automatically:**
- **Discount combination** — tier perks are automatic discounts. If another discount is already on the cart and combination isn't enabled, the perk won't apply. Enable combination on the perk if you want it to stack — but note it will then also stack with sitewide sales, so decide the behaviour you want first.
- **Set maximum discount amount** — cap how much value any single order can take from the perk; a reasonable approach is scaling this cap alongside the tier percentage.
- **Apply discount only once per order** — for fixed-amount perks, this restricts the deduction to once per order total (matching Shopify's native behaviour) instead of the default of applying once per eligible item.

> Note: a one-time "reaching-the-tier" coupon (e.g. free product on Bronze) is configured under **Entry reward**, not here under Privileges/Benefits. See the vip-overview chunk for the entry-reward menu path.

| | Privileges | Entry Rewards |
|---|---|---|
| Frequency | Every qualifying order | One-time |
| Application | Automatic at checkout | Customer redeems |
| Duration | Until tier changes | Single use |

> "One-time" means once per tier-reach. If **Allow giving entry reward again after being downgraded** is enabled (Customer management), a member who drops the tier and later re-reaches it earns the entry reward again. See the "Re-grant entry reward after downgrade" section below.

## Re-grant entry reward after downgrade

By default a tier's **Entry reward** fires only once, the first time a customer reaches that tier. It does **not** fire again if they drop and re-reach the tier — unless this setting is on.

**Setting:** `Allow giving entry reward again after being downgraded` (a checkbox).
**Where:** Joy Admin → **Membership** → **VIP Tiers** → **Tiers** tab → **Tier configuration settings** → **Customer management** (just below "Customize tag prefix", next to "Enable tier point editing").

**What it does (in-app tooltip):** "When enabled, customers who were previously downgraded can receive the entry reward again after re-entering the tier. This applies to downgrades caused by admin adjustments (manual edits or tier imports), tier demotion."

So with this enabled, a member who reaches a tier, drops out of it, then reaches it again **will** receive that tier's entry reward a second time. Covers downgrades from: admin manual edits, tier imports, and natural tier demotion.

## Privilege types

Discount Amount, Discount Percentage, Free Shipping, Free Product, Bonus Points, **Exclusive Products/Collections**, Custom Reward.

Multiple privileges can stack within one tier.

**Free Product perk — Selection Mode:** the Free Product perk supports a **Selection Mode** — instead of the customer always getting one fixed product auto-applied, the merchant defines a product list and lets the customer choose which product(s) they want (and how many) from that list. Configure at **VIP Tiers → [tier] → Tier privileges → Free product → Selection Mode**.

## Periodic (scheduled) perks — Widget V3 only

By default, a tier privilege/perk applies on **every qualifying order, forever** while the customer holds the tier (see the Privileges vs Entry Rewards table above). **Perk Schedule** adds an alternative: the perk resets on a recurring cycle — **weekly, monthly, quarterly, or yearly** — instead of applying continuously. Example: a Gold member can pick 1 free product from a 100-product collection, then gets to pick again every 6 months once the cycle resets.

**Configure at:** VIP Tiers → [tier] → Tier privileges → **Perks → Perk Schedule**.

⚠️ **Widget V3 only.** Perk Schedule currently only works on the legacy **Widget V3** — it is **not yet supported on the Unified Widget (V4)**. If a merchant is on V4 and wants scheduled/periodic perks, tell them this isn't available yet on V4 rather than walking them through the V3 setup path.

## Exclusive products for VIPs

Restrict products/collections so only customers in selected tiers can purchase them. Powered by **Shopify Functions** — runs natively at checkout, no theme hacks. Set up: **Membership → VIP tier → Tier privileges → Add perks → Exclusive products/collections** → choose Collection (recommended) or Product, write **Unlock message** (use `{{tierName}}` placeholder).

Tip: combine with Shopify's **Unlisted** product status to fully hide from storefront. Customers using **Translate & Adapt** should refresh and remove restricted items if switching languages mid-cart.

- Manual assignment only — no auto progression
- Members in exclusive tier **don't progress** through VIP tiers concurrently

## Tier Assessment (rolling-window re-evaluation)

Tier Assessment periodically re-evaluates each customer against a **rolling lookback window** and demotes them if they fall below the maintain threshold — this is how a merchant sets up "keep tier based on spend/orders over the past rolling year".

**Plan:** Available on **Advanced and Ultimate (Enterprise)** only. It is **not** available on the free **Starter** plan or on **Essential (Professional)** — those show a dash in the pricing comparison. So a rolling-tier setup cannot be configured or run on a free plan.

**Also requires enablement by Joy support.** Beyond the plan gate, Tier Assessment sits behind an internal enablement flag (per-shop). A merchant on Advanced/Ultimate who wants it must **contact Joy support to have it turned on for their store** — it is not a self-serve toggle for every shop yet. When a merchant asks for rolling-window tier maintenance, confirm their plan is Advanced or above, then escalate to the team to enable it.

**Reset frequency (updated 2026-08-10):** quarterly is now available as a preset **Reset frequency**, plus a fully custom cycle (2/3/4/6/12 months) with a chosen **Anchor date** — configured in the tier's Assessment/Reset settings, with a **"Next resets"** preview showing the upcoming dates. Changing the frequency only moves the *next* scheduled reset date forward — it does not touch the current tier or point count of any customer at the time of the change.

**On-widget reset date (updated 2026-08-10):** customers now see their reset date without contacting support — **"Tier resets on: {date}"** shows on the tier card in the Customer Account page, and **"Tier progress resets on {date}"** shows under the progress bar on the VIP Tiers widget block. The previous "no on-widget indication" limitation no longer applies.

**Does not apply to Exclusive tiers.** Tier Assessment is built for the standard, automatically-progressing VIP tiers only — **Exclusive tiers** (manually assigned, see the Exclusive Tiers section above) don't auto-progress or auto-demote, so there's no rolling-window renewal/requalification mechanism for them today. A merchant wanting "this ambassador tier must be re-earned every year" has to review and reassign Exclusive-tier members manually; this has been noted as a gap for the product team, not something to promise a workaround for.

## How it works

Configure at **Joy Admin → Membership → VIP Tier → Assessment**. The maintain metric follows the tier's level-up method (**Amount spent**, **Number of orders**, or **Points earned**):

- **Assessment cycle** — how often Joy re-evaluates each customer (e.g. every 12 months) + **Assessment cycle start date** (first day of the cycle)
- **Assessment offset** — the lookback period: the time gap between the assessment date and when the lookback window begins (this is what makes it a *rolling* window, e.g. look back over the past 12 months)
- **Threshold to maintain tier** — the minimum required within the window to keep the tier. The label adapts to the metric: **Spending threshold** (Amount spent), **Order count** (Number of orders), or **Points threshold** (Points earned).

> The exact in-app labels are **Assessment cycle**, **Assessment cycle start date**, **Assessment offset**, and **Spending/Order/Points threshold to maintain tiers**. There is no field literally called "Order Review Timeframe".

## Assessment vs simple demotion

| | Assessment | Demotion |
|---|---|---|
| Trigger | Below maintain threshold across the rolling window | Failed to earn points in period |
| Variables | Cycle + start date + offset + threshold | 1 (cycle) |
| Use case | Rolling spend/order tier maintenance | Simple inactivity downgrade |

# Notifications

Notifications are **off by default** to avoid overwhelming customers. Enable globally then per-program at **Joy Admin → Settings → Notifications** (or **Joy Admin → Notifications**).

## What Joy can notify on

| Area | Triggers |
|---|---|
| Reward programs | Earn points, Redeem points, Birthday rewards, POS redemption |

## Unused Coupon Reminder

Reminds a customer who has redeemed (earned) a coupon but hasn't used it yet, so it doesn't sit unused in their account.

- **Two variants:**
  - **After Redeem** — fires a set number of days after the customer redeems/earns the coupon.
  - **Before Expire** — fires a set number of days before the coupon's expiry date.
- The number of days for each trigger is configurable independently.
- If a customer has multiple unused coupons, they can be grouped into a single reminder email instead of sending one email per coupon.
- Delivery: Joy's own branded email (no external tool needed) at **Notifications → "Coupon Reminder" card**. Merchants on Klaviyo also get two matching Klaviyo trigger events for the same After Redeem / Before Expire logic.

## Email sender options

- **Joy default sender**
- **Simple custom sender** with SPF
- **Custom sender address**
- **Own SMTP** for full control
- **Custom email sending domain**

## Branding

Change brand logo once at **Joy Admin → Settings → Email → Logo** — applies to all notification emails. Customize per-program email content via the block editor (see Email editor below).

## Email editor (block-based)

Each notification email is edited in a drag-and-drop block editor, not a fixed template. **Joy Admin → Settings → Notifications → select a notification** opens the editor full-screen.

- The email is made of independent **blocks** that can be reordered, added, or removed — no fixed logo-top/footer-bottom structure.
- Block types include **Product** (pull in a Shopify product to upsell), **Coupon**, and a **VIP tier progress bar**, plus general content blocks — each block has its own configuration.
- Start from a brand-styled template, preview changes live, and send a test email without leaving the editor.
- **Multi-language in one email:** toggle **Enable email translation** to auto-translate the email into the shop's other enabled languages.
- Shops that had the old flat email template run a one-time data migration to the block format; existing content carries over.

---

Two layers:
1. **Global toggle** — master switch. If off, NO emails send regardless of per-program toggles
2. **Per-program toggle** — fine control once global is on

Start with high-value-only emails:
- Welcome / signup coupon
- Earn confirmation
- Reward redemption coupon
- Points-expiring reminder

Add more if engagement metrics support it. Each email should feel important — avoid spamming.

# Redeeming Programs

Set up at **Joy Admin → Reward programs → Redeeming programs**.

> Plan names below use current naming: **Starter** (free), **Essential**, **Advanced**, **Ultimate**. "Pro" is the legacy name for **Essential** — if any older material says "Pro", read it as Essential.

| Program | Plans |
|---|---|
| Discount (amount, %, BXGY) | All |
| Free gift | Essential, Advanced, Ultimate |
| Free shipping | Essential, Advanced, Ultimate |
| Gift Card | Essential, Advanced, Ultimate |
| Coupon list at checkout | Ultimate (Shopify Plus + Checkout Extensibility) |
| Redeem at checkout page | Ultimate (Shopify Plus + Checkout Extensibility); Advanced via sales contact |
| Total/per-customer redemption limits | All |

When customers redeem, Joy generates a unique one-time-use coupon code.

## How customers actually redeem

The main path is the widget or loyalty page: the customer logs in, opens the widget, goes to **Redeem points**, picks a reward and clicks **Redeem**. They then either click **Apply** to push the code to the cart, or copy the code and paste it at checkout.

**The code does not apply itself at checkout.** This is the single most common "my discount vanished" report — points were spent, the code was issued and is valid, but nobody entered it. Unused codes are always retrievable from the widget's **My coupons** section.

Other redemption surfaces: the **cart drawer** (kb_cart-drawer), **checkout page** (Quick Redeem / coupon list / redeem-at-checkout, see below), and **POS** (staff look up the balance and apply the reward to the cart).

One quirk: if a customer clicks Apply while their cart is empty, the discount is held and takes effect once items are added — the page may need a refresh before the cart reflects it.

**Minimum order value is checked at the moment the coupon is applied at checkout, not at redemption.** So a customer can redeem anytime, but the discount only takes effect once their cart reaches the minimum. Joy displays the minimum automatically wherever the reward appears — e.g. "Applicable for $85 minimum orders" — on the widget, loyalty page, and again in the coupon details under My Rewards after redemption; the condition is never hidden. For Free Gift rewards, merchants can also add their own description to a reward, shown on the widget and loyalty page.

**A redeemed reward is an order-level discount, applied once per order regardless of item quantity.** A merchant with 2+ units of a product in the cart will see the same discount amount as with 1 unit — there is no per-unit multiplication or per-unit cap on a redeemed reward's value. This is expected behaviour, not a bug.

---

## Discount types

- **Discount amount** — fixed $ off
- **Discount percentage** — % off
- **Buy X Get Y (BXGY)** — buy quantity → get extra products/discounts

## Redeem value modes

- **Dynamic Discount** — flexible point thresholds. Optional limits:
  - Minimum points required to redeem
  - Maximum points per redemption
  - Maximum discount % of cart total
- **Fixed Discount** — set $ amount per redemption

## Settings

- **Applicable categories** — products/collections discount applies to
- **Minimum order requirement** — cart minimum
- **Coupon expiration date** — when an individual generated code expires (separate from the reward's own Start/End date, see below)
- **Combinations** — which Shopify discount classes can stack
- **Sales channels** — where the discount is valid

## Redemption program Start/End date

Every redemption program (discount, free gift, free shipping, gift card, etc.) has a **Start/End date** setting, with a **"No end date"** toggle that is **on by default** — existing reward programs keep working unchanged unless a merchant explicitly sets an end date.

- **Start date** — the reward isn't offered for redemption before this date.
- **End date** — once it passes, the reward **automatically hides from new redemption** (customers can no longer redeem it). This is separate from a code's own **Coupon expiration date**: codes customers **already claimed before the end date remain valid** and usable until their own individual expiry — an expired program end date does not retroactively invalidate codes already in customers' hands.
- This is an extension of the older "coupon expiration date" concept: coupon expiration controls when an issued code expires, while Start/End date controls when the reward itself is available to be redeemed at all.

## Reward visibility when restricted to a Shopify customer segment

When a redemption program's **"Who can use this reward"** is set to a specific **Shopify customer segment**, the reward is now **fully hidden from ineligible customers** — it does not appear on the widget, loyalty page, or storefront for anyone outside the segment.

**This is a behavior change.** Previously, a segment-restricted reward was still visible to everyone but blocked/unusable for customers outside the segment. If a merchant or a confused customer asks why a reward "disappeared" even though it used to show up, this is expected: the reward is working as intended, just now hidden instead of shown-but-blocked for non-eligible customers.

---

Available on Essential, Advanced, Ultimate.

## Selection modes

- **Free one product from selection** (default) — customer picks one
- **Free all products in selection** — useful for bundles

**Only products published to the Online Store sales channel sync to Joy and appear in the reward product picker.** Products left as Draft, or removed from the Online Store channel, won't be selectable. If a merchant wants a reward product that shouldn't be publicly browsable: keep the product **Active** in Shopify (it must stay Active for the program to reference it) but hide the Buy button — group reward products under a dedicated product template and hide the Buy button on that template — or combine with a VIP tier perk (**Membership → VIP Tiers → [tier] → Tier privileges → Exclusive products/collections**) to restrict purchase while still allowing point redemption.

### "Too many products/variants" error on a discount program
If a merchant hits a discount-selection limit error even though they picked fewer than 100 **products**, the limit actually counts **variants**, not products — a handful of multi-variant products can add up to 100+ variants quickly. This is a hard cap from **Shopify's own Discount API**, not a Joy setting, and Joy can't raise it. Workaround: group the products into a Shopify **Collection** and select the collection instead of individual products/variants.

## Variants

- For multi-variant products, you can mark specific variants or all as eligible
- If multiple eligible variants are in cart, discount applies to the **lowest-priced variant** automatically

## Settings

Discount combinations, sales channels, usage restrictions (everyone vs only redeemer), coupon expiration, refund-on-cancel, custom code prefix.

Customers select the product in the loyalty widget when redeeming.

---

Essential, Advanced, Ultimate. Same setup as discount: points cost, minimum order, combinations (stack with order/product discounts), sales channels, expiration, refund-on-cancel.

Unused coupons can be revoked and converted back to points by merchant on customer request — **Joy Admin → Customers → [name] → Revoke coupon**.

**Once a coupon has been generated, its conditions and expiry cannot be edited.** If a customer's coupon is about to expire or has expired, the practical fix is to issue a replacement discount code — either revoke and let them re-redeem, or create a code directly in Shopify Admin → Discounts. Expired coupons are automatically hidden from the widget, so customers won't see dead codes.

**Note: changing Combinations only affects newly issued coupons** — codes already in customers' hands keep the settings they were created with.

### Deactivate a coupon WITHOUT refunding points

**Revoke** always converts the unused coupon **back into points** — that is by design, and there is no toggle to "revoke without refund" and no bulk-deactivate in Joy.

- To **disable a code but keep the points spent**, deactivate the code **directly in Shopify → Discounts** (do **not** use Joy's Revoke). Note: after deactivating in Shopify, the coupon's status inside Joy may not auto-update to Expired — if the merchant needs the app status synced, escalate.
- To **deactivate many/all coupons at once without refunding** (e.g. before re-launching a new redeem program), there is no self-serve UI — escalate with the store URL and the list/criteria of coupons to disable. Append `<escalate_human>`.

## Gift Card redeem program

Available on Essential, Advanced, Ultimate.

A **Gift Card** redeem program lets customers exchange points for a **real, reusable Shopify gift card** — not a one-time-use coupon like the other redeem types. The card has its own **balance** and can be spent down gradually across **multiple orders**, just like any gift card issued directly in Shopify.

- **Setup:** **Reward programs → create redeem program → choose type "Gift Card"**. The first time a merchant sets this up, Joy requires granting the app **gift-card permission** in Shopify before the program can be created.
- **On redeem:** the customer can choose to keep the gift card for themselves, or enter a friend's email to send it directly to that person — Shopify sends the gift card to the recipient.
- **Code visibility (security):** the **full gift card code is shown only once**, at the moment of issuance. After that, only the **last 4 digits** are visible — including to the store owner in Shopify Admin. This matches Shopify's own standard gift-card behavior and is not a Joy-specific limitation.

## Send Gift to a Friend (Free Gift rewards)

After a customer redeems a **Free Gift** reward, they get a **"Send to a friend"** option that lets them send the gift coupon directly to someone else — entering the friend's email, name, and a message — instead of, or in addition to, keeping it for themselves.

- **Enable at:** Free Gift program → turn on "Send to Friend" and choose a delivery/automation method.
- **Delivery methods (3):** Joy's built-in email, **Shopify Flow**, or **Klaviyo** — same automation options as Referral. For Joy's built-in email, the template is under **Settings → Notifications → "Send gift to friend"**.
- **Where it appears:** the main widget, loyalty page, My Rewards, and Customer Account.
- **Rate limit (Joy in-app sending only):** fixed at **100 emails/day** total and **1 recipient per 24 hours**, to prevent spam/abuse. This limit is **not merchant-configurable**.

---

Both require **Shopify Plus + Checkout Extensibility** and **Ultimate** plan (Advanced via sales contact).

## Coupon list at checkout

Shows previously redeemed unused coupons inline at checkout. Customer applies in one click. Add via **Reward programs → Redeem programs → [program] → Set up here → Add app block → Joy Coupon List**.

## Redeem at checkout page

Lets customer convert points to discount **directly at checkout**, no widget needed. Toggle on in the program's Redeem value section. Cancel = points refunded instantly.

**Limitation:** Checkout UI extensions don't support i18n by IP/browser. Theme Editor lets you set one main language only.

---

In each program's **Redemption limit** card:
- **Program total limitation** — overall cap (e.g. 50)
- **Each customer's limit** — per-customer cap (optional)

Whichever cap hits first stops further redemptions. When total limit is reached, reward shows **Sold out** in widget. Reset manually via the Reset button next to the counter (cannot be undone). Limits can be edited live without affecting existing redemptions. Only completed redeems count.

## Per-customer limit uses a rolling window (known limitation)
The per-customer / daily redemption limit counts time as a **rolling 24-hour cycle**, not a reset at the store timezone's midnight. So a customer who redeems at 5pm stays locked until 5pm the next day, not until midnight. This can feel unexpected (e.g. locked out at 10am the morning after an evening purchase). There is currently **no merchant-facing setting to switch to a midnight reset** — this is logged product feedback under review by the team. Don't promise a fix date; acknowledge it as a known limitation.

# Product Review Integrations

Set up at **Joy Admin → Reward programs → Write review** (Pro plan required) → choose review app → connect.

## Native / direct integrations (connect inside Joy, no Shopify Flow needed)

| App | Connect fields | How to get them | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Judge.me | None — OAuth redirect | Click Connect in Joy → redirected to Judge.me → authorize | Requires Judge.me's own **Awesome plan or above** for API access |
| Yotpo Reviews | App Key + Secret Key | Yotpo Admin → Settings → General Settings | |
| Air Reviews | App ID (App Key) + Secret Key | Air Reviews → Settings → Manage keys | |
| Fera Product Reviews | Secret Key only | Fera Admin → App & Integrations → API Keys (`app.fera.ai/integrations/api_keys`) | |
| Review Rocket | API Token (UUID) | Generated inside the Review Rocket app | Only review app (with Loox) supporting **separate bonus points for photo vs video** reviews |
| Loox | Public Store ID + Secret Key | Loox Admin → Settings → API Keys | Requires Loox **Convert or Unlimited plan**. After connecting, Joy shows a **webhook URL** (`https://joy.avada.io/app/api/v1/review/loox`) that must be **manually pasted** into Loox Admin → Settings → API Keys → Webhooks (Loox has no auto webhook registration). Also gets the photo/video bonus points feature — separate points for photo vs. video reviews, split config requires Joy **Advanced plan**; see "Loox Review integration" section below for full setup + bonus details. **Merchants who haven't connected this yet still use the old Shopify Flow method** — see Flow table below; connecting flips them over to native. |
| Klaviyo Reviews | None — reuses the shop's existing Klaviyo connection | Connect Klaviyo first at **Joy Admin → Integration → Klaviyo** (Email marketing category); Joy auto-registers the review webhook once Klaviyo is connected | No separate setup step for reviews specifically |

## Shopify Flow integrations (no native connect — merchant builds a Shopify Flow)

| App | Connection method | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Okendo | Shopify Flow template (search "Joy" in Shopify Flow) | |
| Reviews.io | Shopify Flow template (search "Joy" in Shopify Flow) | |
| Growave | Shopify Flow template (search "Joy" in Shopify Flow) | |
| Stamped | Shopify Flow template (search "Joy" in Shopify Flow) | |
| Loox (legacy, not yet connected natively) | Shopify Flow template (search "Joy" in Shopify Flow) | Switches to native automatically once merchant connects Loox directly in Joy (see native table above) |

**How to set up a Flow-based app:** Joy Admin → Reward programs → Write review → select the app → Joy shows a setup guide → merchant builds a Shopify Flow using Joy's **"Add point"** Flow action, triggered by the review app's own Flow trigger (e.g. "review published"). `startDate`/`endDate` fields are disabled for Flow apps since Joy has no visibility into when the review happened; merchant must fill in a **description** field shown on the reward — Joy can't auto-generate it.

---

## Flow (points crediting)

1. Customer submits review via the connected review app
2. **Native apps** (Judge.me, Air, Yotpo, Fera, Loox, Klaviyo Reviews): merchant approves the review → Joy awards points automatically via webhook
3. **Review Rocket**: points awarded on successful submission (no approval step)
4. **Shopify Flow apps** (Okendo, Reviews.io, Growave, Stamped, unconnected Loox): points awarded whenever the merchant's Flow workflow runs, based on the Flow trigger

Note: whether points are credited automatically or need approval in Joy (for native apps) is also governed by **Settings → General → Default status for Product reviews** (Approved = auto, Pending = merchant approves in Review activities). See kb_review-points and kb_settings-general.

## Judge.me "Coupons" feature is NOT Joy points

Judge.me has its own **Coupons** feature that rewards a reviewer with a Judge.me discount code — **entirely separate from Joy points**:
- On each review Judge.me may show **"not eligible for coupon"** or **"this review didn't qualify for a coupon"**. This refers only to Judge.me's coupon, NOT to Joy points.
- It appears on **every** review regardless of Joy point status — including reviews that earned Joy points fine — and typically because the merchant has Judge.me Coupons **Disabled** (which is fine).
- Merchants do **not** need to enable Judge.me Coupons for the Joy integration to work. Joy only needs the OAuth connection at **Joy Admin → Integration → Judge.me**.
- To check whether a review earned Joy points, look at the customer's **Review activities** in Joy — never rely on the Judge.me coupon message.

## Anti-abuse

- Joy honors per-program **fraud prevention** — set **review limit per customer** in the Write Review rule
- Anti-cheat & minimum-character settings (where supported by the review app) apply
- **Joy does NOT reward historical reviews** — only new reviews after the integration is connected

## Reviews tab in the Unified widget (Air Reviews / Judge.me)

The Unified widget has a **Reviews extension** that adds a **"Reviews" tab** so customers review and earn without leaving the widget:
- The tab shows **only the current customer's own reviews** — it does **not** replace the product reviews widget on storefront pages.
- Customers **view their reviews** and **write a new review** directly inside the Joy widget — no redirect away.
- Writing a review **auto-earns points** via the **Write a review** earning rule.
- Reviews render in the **shop's own branding**, with data pulled live from the connected review app.

**Supported review apps for this tab:** **Air Reviews** and **Judge.me** (chosen via the "Review app" radio in the extension). The companion review app must be installed (e.g. an "Install Air Reviews app" prompt shows if it isn't).

**How to turn it on:**
1. Connect the review app first — **Joy Admin → Integration → Air Reviews / Judge.me**.
2. **Joy Admin → On-site content → Widget → Loyalty widget → Setup → Extensions → Reviews** → toggle on, then under **Settings → Review app** pick **Air Reviews** or **Judge.me**.

**Extension settings:**
- **Allow writing reviews from order detail** — shows a "Write a review" button next to purchased products on the order detail page.
- **Image hover effect** — Hover effect off / Swap through images.
- **Review appearance** — e.g. Star rating style.

Loox is **not** one of the two apps supported in this Reviews tab/extension — Loox's integration (below) is about earning bonus points for photo/video reviews, not about embedding a reviews tab in the widget.

## Loox Review integration — connect direct, photo/video bonus

Loox connects **directly inside Joy**, the same as Judge.me and Air Reviews — no Shopify Flow bridge needed (unlike Okendo, Reviews.io, Growave, Stamped, and unconnected Loox setups, which still require building a Shopify Flow — see Flow table above).

**Setup:**
1. Get the **Public Store ID** and **API secret key** from Loox Admin → Settings → API Keys.
2. **Joy Admin → Integration → Loox → Connect.**
3. Finish the **webhook step** following Joy's in-app guide (the webhook URL must be manually pasted into Loox Admin → Settings → API Keys → Webhooks — Loox has no auto webhook registration).
4. **Joy Admin → Reward programs → Write review** → select **Loox** as the review source.

**Photo/video bonus points:**
- Loox rewards can be limited to reviews that include a **photo or video** (smarter targeting than the old Shopify Flow setup, which couldn't filter on this).
- Merchant sets **separate bonus point amounts for photo reviews and video reviews**, then chooses to award **both bonuses** or only the **higher of the two**. This photo/video bonus split configuration **requires Joy Advanced plan**.
- If a customer adds a photo or video to their review **after** their initial (text-only) review, they still receive the bonus **retroactively** — no need to submit a brand-new review.

**Requirements:** Loox plan **Convert or Unlimited** (Loox-side, for API access) + Joy **Advanced plan** (for the photo/video bonus split specifically).

# Joy AI Assistant

In Beta on **Essential and above**. Conversational assistant for app questions, form prep, strategy planning, debugging — without leaving the page.

## Important behavior

Joy AI **does not change settings automatically**. When it wants to configure something, it prepares the form and shows a preview card → you click **Apply** → opens pre-filled form → you save it yourself.

Always verify AI responses before saving — Beta means responses can occasionally be incomplete.

## Opening Joy AI

Click the **magic wand icon (✦)** in the bottom-left of the Joy app. First-time use shows a beta consent modal — click **I understand, let me try**.

## Panel tabs

| Tab | Purpose |
|---|---|
| **Chat** | Main conversation |
| **Canvas** | Persistent doc the AI writes during planning sessions (auto-appears) |
| **Todos** | Multi-step task progress list (auto-appears) |
| **Memory** | What the AI remembers about your store + preferences |

The left sidebar lists conversation threads — create new, rename, delete.

## Use cases

- "How do I set up a birthday reward?"
- "Plan my Q4 loyalty campaign"
- "Why aren't my customers earning points?"
- "Prepare a Place Order rule for 2× points on Summer Collection"

## Related: Shopify Sidekick integration (different from Joy's own AI assistant)

**Shopify Sidekick** is Shopify's own native AI chat inside the Shopify admin — a **separate product** from the Joy AI assistant described above (the magic-wand panel inside the Joy app). Do not conflate the two when a merchant asks about "the AI":

- Joy connects to Sidekick so merchants can ask Sidekick directly about their loyalty program — no need to open the Joy app at all.
- Through Sidekick, merchants can view customer loyalty info (points, tier, rewards, history), see earning/spending programs and VIP tiers, check analytics (revenue, member count, tier distribution), and **adjust customer points or edit a program directly from the Sidekick chat**.
- This differs from Joy AI's own behavior: Joy AI never changes settings automatically (it only prepares a form for the merchant to review and save) — Sidekick, via this integration, can make the change directly in the conversation.
- See <https://help.joy.so/joy-with-shopify-sidekick> for what can be asked/edited and example prompts.
